content.title: About
content.content: Fried cookie is a small sweet pastry made from dough that is deep‑fried until golden and crisp. It has a crunchy texture, buttery aroma and a mild sweetness. Fried cookies are often used as a base for desserts or enjoyed as a standalone snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fried cookies appeared in Europe in the 19th century as an alternative to baked sweets.
The dough typically contains flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and sometimes spices such as cinnamon, ginger or cardamom.
In some countries these treats are called “fritters” and are served dusted with powdered sugar.
Traditionally they are made in small portions, making them ideal for street vendors.
There are many filling variations – from jam and chocolate to nuts and dried fruit.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide quick energy, useful during periods of high activity.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Eggs and dairy in the dough supply a modest amount of animal and plant protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the cookie contains B1, B2 and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Fried cookies provide iron, magnesium and phosphorus, important for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Adding cinnamon or ginger boosts antioxidant content, helping protect cells.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds saturated fats, so consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One cookie can contain 80–120 kcal, which matters for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The dough often contains eggs, milk and gluten, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried cookies warm, dusted with powdered sugar or drizzled with chocolate sauce. They pair well with ice cream, berry coulis, or can be used as a crunchy base for dessert plates.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cookies in an airtight container at room temperature, away from moisture. For longer storage, refrigerate, and for extended periods freeze to preserve their crispness.
